title: AI Cost Monitoring, FinOps & Latency Budgets
description: Track token usage, implement FinOps cost attribution, enforce latency SLOs, and alert on runaway AI spending in .NET.

data.text: The Economics of Generative AI in Production

Unlike traditional software where compute costs scale predictably with CPU and memory, generative AI introduces per-token variable pricing. A single unchecked agent loop or an unoptimized system prompt with bloated few-shot examples can inflate cloud bills by thousands of dollars overnight. Production AI engineering requires strict FinOps practices, token attribution, and latency budgets.

data.title: The Hidden Costs of Multi-Turn Context Windows
data.text: In multi-turn chat applications, prompt token volume grows quadratically if the entire conversation history is blindly resent on every turn. In addition, reasoning models (like OpenAI o1/o3-mini) consume hidden 'reasoning tokens' that are billed at completion token rates. Tracking and caching prompt tokens is essential to maintain sustainable unit economics.

data.text: FinOps Best Practices for .NET AI Teams

items.hint: Cache responses for identical or near-identical user queries using Redis or Azure Cosmos DB vector cache.
Place static system instructions and system guidelines at the very beginning of the prompt to maximize OpenAI/Anthropic prompt cache hits (up to 50% discount).
Enforce maximum monthly token budgets per tenant; send alert emails at 80% and downgrade to lighter models at 100%.
Route simple queries (faq, greetings, intent detection) to lightweight models; invoke reasoning models only when complexity requires it.
Summarize or truncate historical messages older than 10 turns instead of submitting infinite conversation logs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Generative AI operational cost scales by token consumption, demanding active FinOps governance
Establish measurable latency SLOs: Time to First Token (TTFT) and Tokens Per Second (TPS)
Instrument token usage and durations with OpenTelemetry metrics tagged by tenant and model
Leverage prompt caching and semantic caching to reduce redundant LLM invocations
Implement hard and soft budget caps to protect against runaway loops and billing surprises
data.takeaway: Sustainable AI engineering treats cost and latency as first-class architectural constraints. With OpenTelemetry token metrics and semantic caching, .NET teams maintain high performance at predictable costs.
